## Backend Defaults

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-roles.sh from each rule's strength line. Change the rule, then rebuild; do not edit this file. -->

Each line is one rule: its title, its one sentence, and the file that holds it.

- **Build one modular monolith first.** Start a backend as one project or one package split into modules (a module is one feature's folder under `Modules/` or `src/modules/`), and do not start with flat service folders, a giant `common/services`, many tiny packages or projects, or microservice boundaries with no real runtime or deployment boundary. [`backend/build-one-modular-monolith-first.md`]
- **Give each product capability its own module.** Make a module for each real product capability that has its own language, workflow, or lifecycle; an infrastructure concern, a helper, or a detail of another module is not a module. [`backend/give-each-product-capability-its-own-module.md`]
- **Add layers inside a module only when earned.** Inside a module (one feature's folder under `Modules/` or `src/modules/`), use ports (the application-owned types that name a capability), use cases (the Application code for one operation), and domain types only when it has business rules or invariants worth protecting, infrastructure that could realistically vary, orchestration that would be hard to follow inline, or a capability important or brittle enough to need the tests. [`backend/add-layers-inside-a-module-only-when-earned.md`]
- **Use tactical DDD only where complexity earns it.** Use strategic domain-driven design (DDD: bounded contexts, the areas where one model and vocabulary hold; context maps; published language; customer/supplier relationships; anti-corruption layers; and shared kernels, small concepts two or more modules own together) to find boundaries and words, and tactical DDD (aggregates, entities, value objects, domain services, specifications) only where the domain's complexity needs it. [`backend/use-tactical-ddd-only-where-complexity-earns-it.md`]
- **Lay out a dotnet module in the standard shape.** A .NET module is `Modules/<Feature>/` holding `Contracts/` (only when it publishes an API, the types it deliberately exposes to other modules), `Domain/`, `Application/` with `Ports/` (the application-owned types that name a capability) and one folder per use case (the Application code for one operation) holding `<UseCaseName>UseCase.cs`, `Infrastructure/` for adapters (the implementations of ports), and at its root the controller and `<Feature>Module.cs`, with no `Interface/` folder by default. [`backend/lay-out-a-dotnet-module-in-the-standard-shape.md`]
- **Lay out a TypeScript module in the standard shape.** A TypeScript module is `src/modules/<feature>/` holding `contracts/` (only when it publishes an API, the types it deliberately exposes to other modules), `domain/`, `application/` with `ports/` (the application-owned types that name a capability) and one file per use case (the Application code for one operation), placed directly in `application/` or in `application/use-cases/`, `infrastructure/` for adapters (the implementations of ports), `interface/http/<feature>-routes.ts`, and `<feature>.module.ts`. [`backend/lay-out-a-typescript-module-in-the-standard-shape.md`]
- **Register a module in its own module file.** Each module (one feature's folder under `Modules/` or `src/modules/`) registers its own dependencies explicitly in its module file, and the host (the code that assembles the application) supplies only what differs between environments. [`backend/register-a-module-in-its-own-module-file.md`]
- **Put rules in Domain and orchestration in Application.** Domain holds pure rules, invariants, calculations, and decisions; Application holds use cases (the code for one operation), orchestration, ports (the application-owned types that name a capability), transaction boundaries, and what a failure means; Infrastructure holds repositories, HTTP clients, queue and storage adapters, auth provider integrations, and SDK wrappers, and may depend on frameworks and libraries freely. [`backend/put-rules-in-domain-and-orchestration-in-application.md`]
- **Keep framework and transport details out of Application.** Application code carries no framework or transport details. [`backend/keep-framework-and-transport-details-out-of-application.md`]
- **Judge which module needs which from the domain first.** Decide whether one module (a feature folder under `Modules/` or `src/modules/`) needs another from the domain first, from stored data second, and from the code last, because the code is what's under suspicion. [`backend/judge-which-module-needs-which-from-the-domain-first.md`]
- **Redraw a boundary that needs atomic cross-module changes.** When two modules (feature folders under `Modules/` or `src/modules/`) keep needing each other's internal concepts, or one invariant keeps needing atomic changes to both, merge them or redraw the boundary before adding integration ports (the consumer's own types naming a capability it needs) or coordination. [`backend/redraw-a-boundary-that-needs-atomic-cross-module-changes.md`]
- **Put only cross-cutting code in Common.** `Common/` or `shared/` holds only shared code (code no single feature owns): base error types, common middleware and filters, value types that are truly cross-module, and deliberately co-owned shared-kernel contracts (a small concept two or more modules own together); never feature logic or a way round a module boundary (a module is one feature's folder under `Modules/` or `src/modules/`). [`backend/put-only-cross-cutting-code-in-common.md`]
- **Never mirror a module under Common.** `Common/<Feature>/` never mirrors an existing module (one feature's folder, `Modules/<Feature>/` or `src/modules/<feature>/`), even when several modules consume the types; organise shared code by its shared role and keep the types a feature publishes to other modules with the feature. [`backend/never-mirror-a-module-under-common.md`]
- **Keep a port narrow and capability-shaped.** A port names one narrow capability the application needs (something the code needs done for it); it is not a giant service, a mirror of an SDK, or wider than the capability used. [`backend/keep-a-port-narrow-and-capability-shaped.md`]
- **Write a TypeScript port as an abstract class.** Write a port (the Application-owned type that names a capability) as an abstract class with a private constructor and only abstract methods (no fields, no implementation, no static factory), which adapters (the implementations of a port) `implement` and never `extend`. [`backend/write-a-typescript-port-as-an-abstract-class.md`]
- **Share adapter behaviour through functions, not a base class.** When two adapters (implementations of a port) need the same behaviour, put it in pure functions in a shared file that both call, never in a base adapter class. [`backend/share-adapter-behaviour-through-functions-not-a-base-class.md`]
- **Write a use case class only for real orchestration.** Write a use case class (the Application code for one operation) when the flow coordinates several side effects, has sequencing that matters, or is a capability worth naming; for simple procedural behaviour, a direct service method is enough. [`backend/write-a-use-case-class-only-for-real-orchestration.md`]
- **Show a use case's side effects in sequence.** A use case (the Application code for one operation) makes its side effects visible as calls in the order they happen. [`backend/show-a-use-cases-side-effects-in-sequence.md`]
- **Give each read shape a named query.** A repository loads and saves the state a mutation needs; list rows, dropdown options, exports, dashboards, and API read models (the objects the server returns for a screen) each belong to a named query, not to the write repository. [`backend/give-each-read-shape-a-named-query.md`]
- **Never write in a read-named repository method.** A repository method whose name starts with `Get`, `List`, `Find`, `Search`, `Read`, `Query`, `Exists`, or `Count` never adds, updates, deletes, or saves; an operation that reads and writes gets a name that says so. [`backend/never-write-in-a-read-named-repository-method.md`]
- **Call use cases directly without a mediator.** Call a use case through an explicit dependency; do not use MediatR, a command bus, or any ambient dispatcher, because they hide which code runs. [`backend/call-use-cases-directly-without-a-mediator.md`]
- **Declare Command and Result beside the use case.** A use case (the Application code for one operation) declares its Command and Result records (its input and output) as siblings of the use case class in the same file, never nested inside it. [`backend/declare-command-and-result-beside-the-use-case.md`]
- **Declare ExecuteAsync on every use case class.** Every class named `*UseCase` declares `ExecuteAsync`. [`backend/declare-executeasync-on-every-use-case-class.md`]
- **Give every use case a top-level cancellation token.** Every `ExecuteAsync` takes a `CancellationToken` as its own parameter, not nested in another type. [`backend/give-every-use-case-a-top-level-cancellation-token.md`]
- **Pass cancellation from transport to every adapter.** Cancellation flows from the transport layer through Application to every adapter (implementation of a port) call. [`backend/pass-cancellation-from-transport-to-every-adapter.md`]
- **Return Domain outcomes as closed Domain types.** A Domain decision (a rule's verdict on supplied state) with a closed set of meaningful outcomes returns its own result record or sealed outcome type, never an exception and never a general-purpose result type such as FluentResults or a hand-rolled `Result`. [`backend/return-domain-outcomes-as-closed-domain-types.md`]
- **Map a refusal to its failure in one place.** Each decider (the one pure function that guards a lifecycle's actions) has one mapping from its refusal values to the declared failure, which owns the error codes and wording, and every use case (the Application code for one operation) goes through it instead of building the failure at the call site. [`backend/map-a-refusal-to-its-failure-in-one-place.md`]
- **Use one error envelope for every declared failure.** Every declared failure uses the one `ErrorResponse(Code, Message, Errors?)` type, with no `Dto` suffix and no special-purpose variant, so a validation failure is the same envelope with `Errors` filled and the frontend matches on `Code`. [`backend/use-one-error-envelope-for-every-declared-failure.md`]
- **Sign the dev user in with a development handler.** A development environment without real authentication gets a development authentication handler that signs the dev user in. [`backend/sign-the-dev-user-in-with-a-development-handler.md`]
- **Validate at the layer that owns the contract.** Validate each thing once, where its contract is owned: parsing and binding at the transport edge (controllers, endpoints, and the mappers beside them), command shape and meaning in Application, state invariants in Domain, and uniqueness and referential rules in Application backed by database constraints. [`backend/validate-at-the-layer-that-owns-the-contract.md`]
- **Give every validator an explicit error code.** Every FluentValidation validator that can fail declares its own `.WithErrorCode(...)`, because a message or the validator-name default is not a stable code. [`backend/give-every-validator-an-explicit-error-code.md`]
- **Keep entity mapping in the owning module.** Each module (one feature's folder under `Modules/`) configures its own entities in its own Infrastructure; a module never configures another's entities, and mapping is never centralised beside the DbContext. [`backend/keep-entity-mapping-in-the-owning-module.md`]
- **Treat an expected constraint conflict as an outcome.** A constraint conflict the design expects is returned as an outcome, not left to surface as an infrastructure failure. [`backend/treat-an-expected-constraint-conflict-as-an-outcome.md`]
- **Dispatch domain events in process without a queue.** A domain event is an in-memory fact produced by a domain decision; collect and dispatch it explicitly in process, and add durable messaging only when the required consistency crosses the process boundary. [`backend/dispatch-domain-events-in-process-without-a-queue.md`]
- **Put timeouts and retries at Infrastructure boundaries.** Timeouts, retries, and circuit breaking live in the adapter (the implementation of a port) at a volatile boundary. [`backend/put-timeouts-and-retries-at-infrastructure-boundaries.md`]
- **Keep transport retry settings apart from business compensation.** Transport retry settings stay separate from business compensation. [`backend/keep-transport-retry-settings-apart-from-business-compensation.md`]
- **Read time only from the injected clock.** All production code, adapters and SQL included, reads the time from one injected clock, so a test that fixes the clock fixes every comparison. [`backend/read-time-only-from-the-injected-clock.md`]
- **Record telemetry in the layer that owns it.** Transport records request telemetry, Infrastructure records database and external-call telemetry, and an Application operation that is traced or measured carries its business context and is instrumented through a decorator around the use case (the Application code for one operation) rather than scattered log statements. [`backend/record-telemetry-in-the-layer-that-owns-it.md`]
- **Never use a static logger.** Observability keeps dependency direction: no ambient static logger. [`backend/never-use-a-static-logger.md`]
- **Never branch business behaviour on telemetry.** Observability keeps dependency direction: no business behaviour depends on telemetry. [`backend/never-branch-business-behaviour-on-telemetry.md`]
- **Inject ILogger directly without a logging facade.** Inject `ILogger<T>` directly; do not write a custom logging facade. [`backend/inject-ilogger-directly-without-a-logging-facade.md`]
- **Bring secrets in through validated configuration.** A secret enters through validated configuration and never becomes a Domain or Application value unless the use case's job is to operate on that secret. [`backend/bring-secrets-in-through-validated-configuration.md`]
- **Audit security outcomes without sensitive data.** Audit events record security-relevant outcomes and leave out sensitive data. [`backend/audit-security-outcomes-without-sensitive-data.md`]
- **Evolve schemas and contracts by expand and contract.** When old and new versions can run side by side during a deployment, change a database schema or a public contract by expanding first, moving consumers, and contracting last. [`backend/evolve-schemas-and-contracts-by-expand-and-contract.md`]
- **Add to integration messages and version breaking changes.** An integration message (a durable event published across a module or service boundary) is append-only: change it by adding, and give a breaking change an explicit new version. [`backend/add-to-integration-messages-and-version-breaking-changes.md`]
- **Publish shared definitions as immutable versions.** A shared definition that other things consume (a template, list, boundary, type, or schema) has published, immutable versions, and every consumer, its draft included, pins the version it uses and moves to a newer one only by an explicit action that shows what changes. [`backend/publish-shared-definitions-as-immutable-versions.md`]
- **Seal every concrete class.** Mark every concrete C# type `sealed`. [`backend/seal-every-concrete-class.md`]
- **Use records for DTOs, commands, and value objects.** Use a `record` for DTOs, commands, results, and value objects; an EF entity may be a `sealed class`. [`backend/use-records-for-dtos-commands-and-value-objects.md`]
- **Map objects by hand without AutoMapper.** Map between types with explicit code; do not use AutoMapper. [`backend/map-objects-by-hand-without-automapper.md`]
- **Inject dependencies through the constructor.** Domain and Application receive their dependencies as explicit constructor parameters and never take the service provider, and on a TypeScript backend no class fetches a dependency from a locator inside a method. [`backend/inject-dependencies-through-the-constructor.md`]
- **Read environment only in the config owner.** Production source reads the environment only in the root configuration or bootstrap files, and everything else takes the validated config object by injection. [`backend/read-environment-only-in-the-config-owner.md`]
- **Query existence without loading the entity.** When only existence is needed, issue an existence query (`ExistsAsync`, `AnyAsync`) instead of loading the entity. [`backend/query-existence-without-loading-the-entity.md`]
- **Register use cases scoped and caches singleton.** Register use cases as Scoped, and caches and configuration as Singleton. [`backend/register-use-cases-scoped-and-caches-singleton.md`]
- **Run scheduled work off-peak.** Pick a job's time from when its users work, not a round number: batch work (sweeps, reconciliation, rebuilds) runs outside working hours, and work whose result a person sees, such as an email, runs before their day starts, not at its start. [`backend/run-scheduled-work-off-peak.md`]
- **Spread scheduled jobs by a stable hash.** Never start every tenant's or subject's job at the same instant; offset each by a stable hash of its id across a window, so load spreads and a rerun keeps its slot. [`backend/spread-scheduled-jobs-by-a-stable-hash.md`]
- **Name each job's time as a commented constant.** A job's time is a named constant, in the time zone its users live in, with a comment that says why it runs then. [`backend/name-each-jobs-time-as-a-commented-constant.md`]
